summary: Ronald Merry Macphail was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at The Glasgow Academy and the University of Glasgow (~1918–1924, M.B.). He served the Church of Scotland in 1925 and the Bamdah Medical Mission (~1926–1968).

Ronald Morton Smith was an Indologist educated at Bromsgrove School, St Andrews (M.A. 1939), Oxford (B.A./M.A. 1947), and Cambridge (M.A. 1948). He taught at Cambridge (1948–1955) and the University of Toronto (1955–1982), and chaired at Harvard (1976–1978).

Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. His academic career was spent at the University of Calgary, where he served from ~1977 to 2006, including as Associate Professor (~1982–1989), before becoming Professor Emeritus in ~2006.

Ronald S. Green works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at UNC Charlotte, Virginia Tech, Oregon, and UW–Madison, he held positions at UW–Madison (2000–2003), Coastal Carolina University (attested 2013), and ASIANetwork (2020–2025).

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1975–1980). His academic career includes posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1991) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng was a scholar in sinology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at Peking University (~1922–1925) and served on the faculty at Yenching University (~1926–1941).

Rongdao Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, later holding appointments at McGill and the Center for Chinese Studies.

Ronit Ricci is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–1993) and held posts at the Australian National University (2010) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2014).

Ronit Yoeli-Tlalim is a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (1998–2004) and held posts at University College London (attested 2010) and Goldsmiths, University of London (2023–2024).

Roper Lethbridge was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Exeter College (~1859–1863), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1877), and held a fellowship at the University of Calcutta.

Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under the doctoral supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
Rory Mackenzie is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey. He has held a teaching post at International Christian College.

Rosalind Lefeber is an Indologist who completed her doctoral dissertation at the University of Toronto under supervisors Bimal Krishna Matilal and Ronald Morton Smith, and studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She held a post at Toronto (attested 2007).

Rosalind O'Hanlon is a scholar of Indology and history. She earned her PhD at SOAS (~1978–1982), was a fellow at Clare College (~1985–2001), and served as Professor in Indian History and Culture at the University of Oxford (~2001–2019).

Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (1960–1969). He spent his academic career at Komazawa University (1969–2012), becoming a professor in 1983, and served as director of the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

Rosane Rocher is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher at Université libre de Bruxelles (MA ~1955–1959). She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1961–1970) and as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (from 1970).

Rosemarie Fuchs is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg and completed her Habilitation at Regensburg. She held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994) and Jena (1994–2013), and served as president of Indogermanische Gesellschaft (2004–2016).
Rosemary Radford Ruether was a religious studies scholar who studied at the Claremont School of Theology (~1959–1965) and held an academic post at Howard University (~1965–1976).

Rosina Pastore works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Naples, Visva-Bharati, and Lausanne (PhD 2016–2022) under Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere. She held posts at the University of Lausanne (2016–2022) and Ghent University (2022–2025).
